name.ar: مسرّعة Startmate — دورة صيف 2027

deadline_note: Official page: applications close 11:59pm AEDT, Sunday 1 November 2026; Startmate runs a Winter cohort too, so a missed deadline means waiting ~6 months.

summary.en: Australia and New Zealand's best-known startup accelerator invests A$120k in each team, with no programme fees. The Summer '27 cohort is remote-first with three in-person weeks in Melbourne.
summary.ka: ავსტრალიისა და ახალი ზელანდიის ყველაზე ცნობილი აქსელერატორი თითო გუნდში 120 ათას ავსტრალიურ დოლარს აბანდებს, საფასურის გარეშე. ზაფხული '27-ის ნაკადი ძირითადად დისტანციურია, მელბურნში სამი კვირით.
summary.ar: أشهر مسرّعة للشركات الناشئة في أستراليا ونيوزيلندا تستثمر 120 ألف دولار أسترالي في كل فريق دون أي رسوم. دورة صيف 2027 عن بُعد في معظمها مع ثلاثة أسابيع حضورية في ملبورن.

about.en:
Startmate is a founder-led accelerator for the Australia and New Zealand ecosystem. The Summer '27 programme runs for 14 weeks from 1 February to 7 May 2027. It is remote-first on Australian time, with in-person weeks for Week 0 in Melbourne, a mid-programme week and Demo Day week.

It is open to any stage, from idea to early revenue, in any industry; solo founders are welcome. Founders can join from anywhere in Australia or New Zealand, or from overseas if they have a strong connection to ANZ, which makes it relevant for international students and graduates of Australian or NZ universities who are building a company.

Each accepted startup receives A$120k at acceptance (A$120k for 8% at a A$1.5m post-money valuation if you have not raised before), plus mentoring from Startmate's network of founders and operators.

en: A$120k investment at acceptance, no programme fees
Remote-first: only three in-person weeks
Idea-stage teams accepted; 67% had no revenue when they applied

eligibility.en: Founders of any age based in Australia or New Zealand, or overseas founders with a strong connection to ANZ. At least one founder must be (or become) full-time. Any industry, any stage.

en: Read the accelerator page and FAQs on startmate.com/accelerator.
Create an account on Startmate Universe and complete the online application before 11:59pm AEDT on 1 November 2026.
Shortlisted teams are interviewed; offers go out in mid-December 2026.
Attend Week 0 in Melbourne on 1 February 2027.

costs.en: No programme fee. Startmate invests A$120k (SAFE or priced round). Travel to the in-person weeks is at your own cost.

score_reason: Strong, funded accelerator but the deadline is 1 Nov 2026 and it needs an ANZ link.

name.ar: معسكر Startmate للطلاب المؤسسين 2027 (سيدني وملبورن)

deadline_note: Applications (expressions of interest) open in November 2026; closing date not yet published on the official page.

summary.en: A two-day overnight bootcamp in Sydney or Melbourne that teaches university students how to start a startup. No experience needed; A$200 covers food and accommodation.
summary.ka: ორდღიანი ბუთქემპი სიდნეიში ან მელბურნში, სადაც უნივერსიტეტის სტუდენტები სტარტაპის წამოწყებას სწავლობენ. გამოცდილება საჭირო არ არის; 200 ავსტრალიური დოლარი კვებასა და საცხოვრებელს ფარავს.
summary.ar: معسكر لمدة يومين مع مبيت في سيدني أو ملبورن يعلّم طلاب الجامعات كيفية تأسيس شركة ناشئة. لا تُشترط خبرة سابقة؛ ورسوم 200 دولار أسترالي تشمل الطعام والإقامة.

about.en:
The Student Founder Bootcamp is Startmate's entry-level programme for university students who are curious about building a startup. Two editions run in March 2027, one in Sydney and one in Melbourne, each over two days with an overnight stay.

It is open to all university students across Australia and New Zealand, including international students enrolled there, and no prior experience is required. Participants work on ideas with experienced founders and meet other ambitious students; it is a common first step towards Startmate's fellowships and accelerator.

en: Two days in person with experienced startup founders
Open to any degree, no experience required
Low fee (A$200) covers accommodation and food

eligibility.en: Students currently enrolled at a university in Australia or New Zealand (domestic or international). No age limit or prior startup experience required.

en: Open the Student Founder Bootcamp page on startmate.com.
Submit the 'Express Interest' form; full applications open in November 2026.
Wait for the outcome, sent shortly after applications close.
Pay the A$200 fee and travel to Sydney or Melbourne in March 2027.

costs.en: A$200 including GST, covering accommodation and food. Travel to Sydney/Melbourne is at your own cost.

score_reason: Cheap, beginner-friendly, but only for students already at ANZ universities.

name.ar: مسرّعة Iterative — دفعة شتاء 2027 (جنوب شرق آسيا)

deadline_note: Official apply page lists the Winter 2027 batch (Feb–May 2027) but no fixed deadline; it offers an email reminder one month before the deadline.

summary.en: Singapore-based Iterative invests US$150k–500k in Southeast Asian startups twice a year, paid upfront with no programme fees. The Winter 2027 batch starts with a 4-day in-person orientation and continues remotely.
summary.ka: სინგაპურული Iterative წელიწადში ორჯერ სამხრეთ-აღმოსავლეთ აზიის სტარტაპებში 150–500 ათას აშშ დოლარს აბანდებს, წინასწარ და საფასურის გარეშე. 2027 ზამთრის ნაკადი 4-დღიანი ორიენტაციით იწყება და დისტანციურად გრძელდება.
summary.ar: تستثمر Iterative ومقرها سنغافورة ما بين 150 و500 ألف دولار أمريكي في الشركات الناشئة في جنوب شرق آسيا مرتين سنويًا، تُدفع مقدمًا دون رسوم. تبدأ دفعة شتاء 2027 بتوجيه حضوري لأربعة أيام ثم تستمر عن بُعد.

about.en:
Iterative is a Singapore-based accelerator and seed fund focused on founders building in Southeast Asia. Twice a year it runs a batch; the Winter 2027 batch runs from February to May 2027, beginning with a four-day in-person orientation, after which founders stay in their home market and work remotely with the partners.

It invests in all industries and stages, including startups that are only an idea, assessing market, evidence and founders. Student and recent-graduate founders building for Southeast Asian markets are eligible.

Each company receives US$150,000–500,000 for roughly 10–15%, paid in full on admission with no milestones, clawbacks or programme fees.

en: US$150k–500k invested upfront, no fees
Idea-stage startups can apply
Remote after a 4-day in-person orientation

eligibility.en: Founders (any nationality) building startups for Southeast Asian markets. Only founders may attend interviews and batch events. No minimum traction required.

en: Read the batch details on iterative.vc/apply.
Sign up for the deadline reminder and prepare a short written application about your market, evidence and team.
Submit the online application for the Winter 2027 batch.
Shortlisted founders are interviewed by the partners.

costs.en: No programme fee. Investment of US$150k–500k for about 10–15% equity. Travel to the orientation at your own cost.

score_reason: Large cheques and idea-stage friendly, but deadline not yet published and SEA focus.

name.ar: مسابقة الرياضيات الأسترالية (AMC) 2027

duration.ka: ერთი წერითი ტური, 60–75 წუთი (2027 წლის 3–5 აგვისტო)

deadline_note: Official AMC page: printed-paper entries from outside Australia/NZ close Friday 25 June 2027; online entries close 30 July 2027.

summary.en: One of the world's largest school maths competitions, sat in schools in Australia and internationally. Schools register students in divisions from Year 1 to Year 12 for about AUD 9.30 each.
summary.ka: მსოფლიოს ერთ-ერთი უდიდესი სასკოლო მათემატიკური კონკურსი, რომელსაც ავსტრალიასა და სხვა ქვეყნების სკოლებში წერენ. სკოლა მოსწავლეებს 1–12 კლასების დივიზიონებში არეგისტრირებს, თითოზე დაახლოებით 9.30 ავსტრალიური დოლარი.
summary.ar: إحدى أكبر مسابقات الرياضيات المدرسية في العالم، تُجرى في المدارس داخل أستراليا وخارجها. تسجّل المدارس طلابها في فئات من الصف الأول إلى الثاني عشر بنحو 9.30 دولار أسترالي للطالب.

about.en:
The Australian Mathematics Competition (AMC), run by the Australian Mathematics Trust since 1978, is a problem-solving contest taken by hundreds of thousands of students. The 2027 competition is sat at school between Tuesday 3 and Thursday 5 August 2027, on paper or online.

Divisions: Middle Primary (Years 3–4), Upper Primary (5–6), Junior (7–8), Intermediate (9–10) and Senior (11–12), plus a new Early Primary division for Years 1–2 from 2027. International schools can enter, with an earlier deadline for printed papers sent abroad.

Every student gets a result and certificate; top scorers receive prizes and medals, and a strong AMC score is a useful early signal for national olympiad pathways.

en: Taken by students in dozens of countries
Paper or online, sat at your own school
Certificates for all, medals for top scorers

eligibility.en: School students in Years 1–12. Entry is through a registered school (in Australia, New Zealand or internationally); students cannot usually enter alone.

en: Ask your school maths coordinator to register on the AMT admin portal (competitions.amt.edu.au/admin).
International printed entries must be registered by 25 June 2027; online entries by 30 July 2027.
Sit the paper at school between 3 and 5 August 2027.
Results and certificates are released by AMT after marking.

costs.en: AUD 9.30 per student (bundle discounts available); paid by the school.

score_reason: Cheap, school-based and widely available, but needs school registration.

org: Center for iPS Cell Research and Application (CiRA), Kyoto University

name.ar: برنامج التدريب البحثي في CiRA لعام 2027 (جامعة كيوتو)

deadline_note: Estimated: overseas deadline was 6 Feb 2026 (5pm JST) and is set around early February every year; confirm on the official page.

summary.en: Work for up to six weeks in a stem-cell lab at Kyoto University's CiRA, founded by Nobel laureate Shinya Yamanaka. Travel and accommodation are partly covered.
summary.ka: იმუშავეთ ექვს კვირამდე ღეროვანი უჯრედების ლაბორატორიაში კიოტოს უნივერსიტეტის CiRA-ში, რომელიც ნობელის ლაურეატმა შინია იამანაკამ დააარსა. მგზავრობა და საცხოვრებელი ნაწილობრივ იფარება.
summary.ar: اعمل حتى ستة أسابيع في مختبر للخلايا الجذعية في مركز CiRA بجامعة كيوتو الذي أسسه الحائز على نوبل شينيا ياماناكا، مع تغطية جزئية للسفر والسكن.

about.en:
CiRA is Kyoto University's centre for induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell research. Its Research Internship Program lets students spend 1–6 consecutive weeks in a host lab between June and October, joining lab work, doing basic experiments and presenting their results at the end.

It is aimed mainly at third- and fourth-year undergraduates and graduate students who may later join CiRA as graduate students or postdocs. Each lab takes at most one overseas student, so places are few and competitive.

CiRA covers a round trip to Kyoto (partly) and accommodation up to JPY 5,500 per day. Overseas students pay a short-term student fee (JPY 29,700/month in 2026) unless their university has an exchange agreement with Kyoto University.

en: Lab placement at a world-leading stem-cell institute
Partial travel and accommodation support
Pathway to graduate study at Kyoto University

eligibility.en: Undergraduates (mainly 3rd–4th year) and graduate students at overseas universities, planning to start graduate school within one or two years. Any nationality. English is the working language in most labs.

en: Read the internship page and the list of host PIs; email a host PI before applying (recommended).
Fill in the application form and written pledge, and get consent from your home supervisor.
Submit by the overseas deadline (early February).
Results are announced around the end of March.
Arrange personal accident and liability insurance before arrival.

costs.en: Round trip and accommodation (up to JPY 5,500/day) partly covered. Short-term student fee of JPY 29,700/month for overseas students (waived for Kyoto University partner institutions). No stipend.

score_reason: Prestigious and partly funded; small number of overseas places.

org: The University of Tokyo — Graduate School of Frontier Sciences

name.ka: ტოკიოს უნივერსიტეტის საზაფხულო სტაჟირება UTSIP Kashiwa 2027
name.ar: برنامج التدريب الصيفي لجامعة طوكيو UTSIP Kashiwa 2027

deadline_note: Estimated: the 2026 deadline was 13 January 2026, 17:00 Tokyo time; the 2027 call is expected on the same pattern.

summary.en: A summer research internship on the University of Tokyo's Kashiwa campus for undergraduates enrolled at overseas universities. Interns join a Frontier Sciences lab for the summer.
summary.ka: საზაფხულო კვლევითი სტაჟირება ტოკიოს უნივერსიტეტის კაშივას კამპუსზე უცხოურ უნივერსიტეტებში ჩარიცხული ბაკალავრებისთვის. სტაჟიორები ზაფხულს Frontier Sciences-ის ლაბორატორიაში ატარებენ.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي صيفي في حرم كاشيوا التابع لجامعة طوكيو لطلاب البكالوريوس المسجلين في جامعات خارج اليابان، حيث ينضم المتدربون إلى مختبر في كلية العلوم الحدودية.

about.en:
UTSIP Kashiwa is the Graduate School of Frontier Sciences' summer internship for undergraduate students enrolled at overseas universities. Interns spend the summer in a lab on the Kashiwa campus near Tokyo, in fields such as materials, environmental studies, biosciences, computational biology, ocean technology and complexity science.

It is a way to experience graduate-level research at Japan's top university and to meet potential supervisors for a master's or PhD. The 2026 call closed on 13 January 2026; the 2027 call is expected to open in late 2026 with a similar January deadline.

Support in past cycles has included a scholarship/allowance and help with housing; check the 2027 call for exact amounts.

en: Research at the University of Tokyo
Specifically for undergraduates at overseas universities
Strong route into UTokyo graduate admissions

eligibility.en: Undergraduate students currently enrolled at a university outside Japan, in science or engineering fields relevant to Frontier Sciences labs. Any nationality.

en: Watch the Frontier Sciences news page for the UTSIP Kashiwa 2027 announcement (late 2026).
Pick host labs from the list in the call.
Prepare transcripts, a statement of purpose and recommendation as requested.
Submit before the January deadline (17:00 Tokyo time).

costs.en: Check the 2027 call: past cycles offered support towards living costs; travel is usually at your own cost.

score_reason: Top university, open to all nationalities; 2027 details not yet published.

name.ar: برنامج الباحث المشارك الدولي في RIKEN (IPA) — دعوات 2027

deadline_note: Official page: calls for overseas applicants open every April and September; exact 2027 deadlines are set in each call.

summary.en: RIKEN, Japan's largest research institute, hosts non-Japanese PhD students in its labs for one to three years. Airfare, a daily allowance of JPY 5,200 and housing are covered.
summary.ka: RIKEN, იაპონიის უდიდესი კვლევითი ინსტიტუტი, არაიაპონელ დოქტორანტებს ერთიდან სამ წლამდე მასპინძლობს. იფარება ავიაბილეთი, დღიური 5,200 იენი და საცხოვრებელი.
summary.ar: يستضيف معهد RIKEN، أكبر مؤسسة بحثية في اليابان، طلاب الدكتوراه غير اليابانيين في مختبراته لمدة سنة إلى ثلاث سنوات، مع تغطية تذكرة الطيران وبدل يومي 5,200 ين والسكن.

about.en:
The International Program Associate (IPA) programme lets non-Japanese doctoral students carry out their PhD research at RIKEN (Wako, Kobe, Yokohama, Harima and other campuses) under a RIKEN supervisor, through RIKEN's joint graduate school partnerships with universities in Japan and abroad.

Placements usually last one to three years and start in October or April. Applicants first find a RIKEN researcher willing to host them; the researcher contacts RIKEN's personnel office, and the student then applies in the April or September call.

RIKEN covers one round-trip airfare, a living allowance of JPY 5,200 per day, free on-campus housing (or up to JPY 70,000/month rent) and accident insurance.

en: Fully funded PhD research at a world-class institute
Housing plus JPY 5,200/day allowance
Calls twice a year (April and September)

eligibility.en: Non-Japanese PhD students enrolled at a Japanese or overseas university that has (or is signing) a joint graduate school agreement with RIKEN. A RIKEN host researcher must agree to supervise you.

en: Browse RIKEN labs and contact a researcher whose work matches yours.
If they agree to host you, they notify RIKEN's Research Personnel Affairs Section.
Apply in the April or September call with the documents requested.
Pass RIKEN screening and internal approval; start in October or April.

costs.en: Covered: one round-trip airfare, JPY 5,200/day living allowance, free housing or rent up to JPY 70,000/month, accident insurance. No fees.

score_reason: Fully funded, but only for PhD students at partner universities with a host secured.

name.en: University of Seoul International Research Internship — Summer 2027
name.ka: სეულის უნივერსიტეტის საერთაშორისო კვლევითი სტაჟირება — ზაფხული 2027
name.ar: برنامج التدريب البحثي الدولي في جامعة سيول — صيف 2027

deadline_note: Estimated from the 2026 cycle (preliminary application by email by 27 March 2026, summer session 1 July – 21 August); confirm the 2027 call.

summary.en: A credit-bearing summer research internship in University of Seoul labs, with on-campus housing and field trips included. Aimed at students from UOS partner universities, with a non-partner fee also listed.
summary.ka: კრედიტიანი საზაფხულო კვლევითი სტაჟირება სეულის უნივერსიტეტის ლაბორატორიებში, კამპუსის საცხოვრებლითა და ექსკურსიებით. განკუთვნილია პარტნიორი უნივერსიტეტების სტუდენტებისთვის, თუმცა არაპარტნიორთა საფასურიც მითითებულია.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي صيفي معتمد بساعات دراسية في مختبرات جامعة سيول، يشمل السكن الجامعي والرحلات الثقافية. موجّه لطلاب الجامعات الشريكة مع رسوم محددة لغير الشركاء أيضًا.

about.en:
The UOS International Research Internship places international students in University of Seoul labs for at least 160 hours of research during the 7.5-week summer session (SISS I), earning 3 credits. Labs in engineering, science, urban studies and other fields post their own projects and requirements (some ask for TOEFL 100 or TOPIK 5, a CV and an interview).

The 2026 timeline was: preliminary email application by 27 March, online interviews in early April, results by mid-April, then official summer-session application and payment. The 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern.

The fee includes on-campus housing and cultural field trips, which makes it a practical, structured way to try research in Korea.

en: 3 credits for 160+ hours of lab research
Housing and cultural trips included in the fee
Seoul location with semester-long option too

eligibility.en: Students from UOS global partner universities (the page also lists a non-partner fee). Each lab sets its own requirements on major and English/Korean level; some positions are for graduate students only.

en: Check the OIA International Research Internship page for the 2027 lab list.
Email your preliminary application to uosinternship@uos.ac.kr by the late-March deadline.
Attend an online interview in early April.
If selected, complete the official summer session application and pay via Flywire.

costs.en: 2026 fee: KRW 2,400,000 (partner students) or KRW 2,600,000 (non-partners), including on-campus housing and field trips. No stipend.

score_reason: Structured and affordable, but aimed at partner universities and paid.

org: Keio University — Human Biology-Microbiome-Quantum Research Center (Bio2Q)

name.en: Keio University Bio2Q Research Internship Program 2027
name.ar: برنامج التدريب البحثي Bio2Q في جامعة كيو 2027

deadline_note: Official page: deadline 1 December 2026, 23:59 JST; final results around February 2027.

summary.en: A funded 8–12 week research internship at Keio University's Bio2Q centre in Tokyo, covering human biology, microbiome and quantum computation. Housing and travel are supported and no Japanese is needed.
summary.ka: დაფინანსებული 8–12-კვირიანი კვლევითი სტაჟირება კეიოს უნივერსიტეტის Bio2Q ცენტრში ტოკიოში: ადამიანის ბიოლოგია, მიკრობიომი და კვანტური გამოთვლები. საცხოვრებელი და მგზავრობა ფინანსდება, იაპონური არ არის საჭირო.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي ممول لمدة 8–12 أسبوعًا في مركز Bio2Q بجامعة كيو في طوكيو، يشمل بيولوجيا الإنسان والميكروبيوم والحوسبة الكمية، مع دعم للسكن والسفر ودون الحاجة إلى اللغة اليابانية.

about.en:
Bio2Q is a World Premier International Research Center (WPI) at Keio University that combines human biology, microbiome science and quantum computation. Its 2027 Research Internship Program hosts students in Bio2Q labs for 8–12 weeks between 10 May and 10 August 2027, with exact dates agreed with the host lab.

It targets students who are considering a master's or PhD at Keio: bachelor's and master's students for the Graduate School of Medicine, and master's students for Science and Technology or Pharmaceutical Sciences. Recent graduates may also apply, and English is the working language.

Bio2Q provides designated accommodation and travel expenses (subject to conditions). Selection is by document review and an online interview, with results around February 2027.

en: Housing and travel covered
English-only, no prior lab contact needed
Cutting-edge mix of microbiome, medicine and quantum computing

eligibility.en: Bachelor's and master's students (or recent graduates) worldwide aiming at Keio's Graduate School of Medicine; master's students aiming at a PhD in Science and Technology or Pharmaceutical Sciences. No Japanese or language certificate required if you communicate in English.

en: Read the 2027 guidelines PDF on the Bio2Q news page.
Choose up to three labs in the Keio Web Entry System and write one Statement of Purpose.
Submit documents online (or by email) by 1 December 2026, 23:59 JST.
Attend an online interview if shortlisted; final results around February 2027.

costs.en: Designated accommodation and travel expenses are provided (travel subject to conditions). No stipend or living allowance.

score_reason: Open worldwide, funded housing and travel, deadline 1 Dec 2026.

name.en: Kyoto University KU-STAR Program for India 2027
name.ar: برنامج KU-STAR لجامعة كيوتو للهند 2027

deadline_note: Estimated: the 2026 deadline was 27 January 2026 (5pm JST) for a May–July internship; check the KU-STAR page for the 2027 call.

summary.en: A summer research internship in Kyoto University labs for students enrolled at universities in India who want to do a PhD in Kyoto. Accommodation is provided by the university.

It is free to enter and a strong line on a CV for student entrepreneurs, with networking with Chinese investors and universities.

about.en:
Global Village is Habitat for Humanity's short-term volunteer travel programme. On this trip (4–11 September 2027) a team of international volunteers works alongside a local family, a building contractor and community volunteers. The team helps build a one-bedroom, one-bathroom home of about 28 m², mixing cement, wiring rebar, laying foundations, erecting walls and laying bricks.

The week typically runs: arrival, orientation and welcome dinner, four to five build days (with one cultural/social learning exchange activity), a farewell and home dedication, then departure. No construction experience is needed; work can be strenuous, so volunteers should be in good health.

The programme donation (US$2,095) covers shared hotel rooms, meals and in-country costs and supports the family's home; flights are extra. It is a meaningful volunteering experience for students and families and a good topic for university application essays.

Sessions cover planning a research strategy from identifying needs to producing output, qualitative and quantitative methods, critical reading of statistical analysis and professional research writing, plus a 'Master Series' session, a capstone and a session on research postgraduate studies at HKU.

It is open to current bachelor's and master's students from recognised universities anywhere, and suits students thinking about an MPhil or PhD. Applicants write a 200–300 word statement and may be interviewed.

It is non-credit bearing (certificate of attendance); optional HKU residential hall accommodation is available.

TSSP is Tohoku University's four-week summer programme for freshman and sophomore science and engineering students. It combines lectures on frontier science and technology, disaster science based on the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, hands-on group experiments, and Japanese language and culture. In 2026 it ran from 21 June to 18 July.

Applicants must be full-time undergraduates at a listed partner institution in Australia, Canada, China, Singapore, the UK or the USA, nominated by their home university. Completers receive the equivalent of 8 ECTS credits (transfer decided by the home university).

A JASSO scholarship of JPY 80,000 is available to outstanding students who meet JASSO requirements.

The Global Young Scientists Summit (GYSS), organised by Singapore's National Research Foundation, brings together young scientists and leading minds from around the world under the theme 'Transcending Borders'. The 2027 summit takes place from 4 to 8 January 2027 in Singapore.

The format includes plenary lectures, panel huddles, quickfire pitches, fireside chats and site visits to Singapore research institutes, with close interaction with Nobel laureates, Fields Medallists, Turing Award winners and other eminent scientists.

Participants (mainly PhD students and early postdocs in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and medicine) attend through nomination by GYSS partner universities and research institutions worldwide.

about.en:
Indonesia International Applied Science Project Olympiad (I2ASPO) is an international science, invention and innovation fair run by the Indonesian Young Scientist Association (IYSA), which organises project competitions for students from elementary school to university in Indonesia and with partners in many countries. I2ASPO challenges students to create work that can be applied directly to benefit society and to find solutions to problems in their own environment.

Participants (individually or in small teams) submit a research or invention project in one of the categories (waste treatment, IoT, functional food, energy, research on children with special needs, entrepreneurship, physics and engineering, applied social, environmental and life sciences) and present it to a panel of judges, either in person in Indonesia or online. Medals (gold, silver, bronze) and special awards are given, and all participants receive certificates.

It is an accessible way for school and university students to present their first research project internationally. The guidebook on the official website gives the venue, fees and rules.

about.en:

about.en:
ICAS (originally the International Competitions and Assessments for Schools, developed at UNSW) are annual academic competitions sat online at school. Subjects are Mathematics, English, Science, Writing, Digital Technologies and the Spelling Bee, for students from Year 2 to Year 12.

In 2026 the sitting windows ran through August (Digital Technologies and Writing 3–7 Aug, English 10–14 Aug, Science 17–21 Aug, Mathematics 24–28 Aug), with entries closing in late July. The 2027 calendar is expected to follow the same pattern.

Every student receives a detailed individual report; top performers receive High Distinction certificates and medals. Schools in Australia, New Zealand, Asia and other regions take part, and parents can enter through the school's parent payment system.

en: Six subjects for Years 2–12
Detailed skills report for every student
Medals for top scorers internationally

eligibility.en: School students in Years 2–12 at participating schools (Australia, New Zealand, Asia and elsewhere; India via a separate ICAS India site). Entry is through the school.

en: Ask your school whether it runs ICAS, or ask it to register.
Enter through the school or the Parent Payment System before the July closing date.
Sit each subject online at school in its August window.
Receive results and certificates later in the year.

costs.en: 2026: from AUD 21.95 per student per subject; 2027 fees to be published.

score_reason: Widely available school competition; 2027 dates estimated.

about.en:
The World Masters Games are the world's largest multi-sport event for adult athletes (roughly 30 and over). The 2027 edition is hosted across the Kansai region of Japan (Osaka, Kyoto, Hyogo, Shiga, Nara, Wakayama and more), opening on 14 May 2027.

Volunteers support venues, athlete services and visitors in a chosen prefecture or city. You pick a location and activity from the volunteer page and apply through that local committee; each committee sets its own details and deadlines.

Volunteers must be 18 or older on 1 April 2027, speak everyday conversational Japanese, attend common and role-specific training, work 5–8 hours a day and arrange their own lodging and transport. It suits international students already living in Japan; a uniform is provided and can be kept afterwards.

en: Be part of a major international sports event in Japan
Uniform provided (yours to keep)
Choose your city and role across Kansai

eligibility.en: Aged 18+ as of 1 April 2027; everyday conversational Japanese; able to attend training and work 5–8 hours a day. Nationality not restricted, but lodging and transport are self-arranged, so best for residents of Japan.

en: Open the volunteer page on wmg2027.jp.
Choose a prefecture or city and activity from the banners.
Apply through that local committee's application page before its deadline.
Attend the common and role-specific training sessions.

costs.en: Free to volunteer. Uniform provided. Lodging and transport are at your own cost.

score_reason: Real volunteering role but requires Japanese and self-funded stay.

summary.ar: مدرسة صيفية لأربعة أسابيع في الكلية الدولية الرائدة في تايلاند، تقدّم مقررات معتمدة في الاستدامة والطب الاستوائي وعلم النفس والأعمال والتصميم والثقافة التايلاندية، ومفتوحة لطلاب البكالوريوس من أي جامعة.

about.en:
The MUIC Summer Program runs on Mahidol University's Salaya campus near Bangkok from 1 to 30 July 2027. Option 1, 'Sustainable in Actions', is an all-day Practical Sustainability and Biodiversity course with overnight field visits. Option 2 offers 4-credit courses: The Psychology of Emotional Well-being, Perspectives on Thailand, Introduction to Thai Language and Culture, Diversity and Expatriate Management, International Design Language and Culture, Introduction to Tropical Medicine, and Social and Health Issues in Thailand.

It is open to undergraduates who have completed at least one semester (or recent graduates) from any university worldwide. Extras include Muay Thai, Thai cooking and dance, a day trip to Ayutthaya, airport transfers, and help with visa letters and housing.

Courses earn a digital transcript, so credits can often be transferred to your home university.

en: Credit-bearing courses including tropical medicine and global health
Open to undergraduates from any university
Cultural programme: Muay Thai, Thai cooking, Ayutthaya trip

eligibility.en: Undergraduates who have completed at least one semester, or recent graduates, from any country. IELTS 5.5 or equivalent for non-native English speakers (or a recommendation letter from an English professor).

en: Fill in the online application form on the MUIC Summer Program page (from 1 November 2026).
Upload passport page, transcript, English proof (or recommendation) and photo.
Pay the invoice within 15 days and email proof to icshortterm@mahidol.ac.th.
Receive the acceptance and visa letters from MUIC.

costs.en: Option 1: THB 82,500 (about USD 2,500) including shared accommodation. Option 2: THB 33,500 for one course or THB 62,000 for two (accommodation not included). Fees include tuition, visits, transcript, airport transfers and welcome/farewell meals; flights and insurance extra.

score_reason: Open to all, affordable, credit-bearing and well documented.

about.en:
SEED (Sustainable English Experiential Discovery) is run by the Language Institute of Chiang Mai University as part of its Global Sustainability School. The spring 2027 edition runs from 7 to 20 February 2027 in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand.

Participants study English and public speaking while learning about SDG 6 (water security), climate change, flooding and community resilience. The programme includes Lanna culture, Thai cooking, a visit to Doi Suthep, a Khantoke dinner and a CMU student buddy.

It is open to international undergraduate and postgraduate students (and faculty-led groups); no sustainability background is needed.

en: Sustainability and English skills in northern Thailand
CMU student buddy and cultural activities
13 nights accommodation included

eligibility.en: International undergraduate and postgraduate students (individuals or groups). No sustainability background required.

en: Read the programme details on the Global Sustainability School page.
Submit the online Apply Now form.
Wait for confirmation and payment instructions from LICMU.
Arrange flights, insurance and visa for Thailand.

costs.en: THB 37,500 including programme fees, 13 nights accommodation, logistics and some meals. Flights and insurance extra.

score_reason: Affordable and open, but short and language-focused.

Women Leading Our Connected World (WOW) is a Chiang Mai University Language Institute programme focused on women's empowerment, leadership and intercultural communication, run from 28 August to 13 September 2027 in Chiang Mai.

It is part of CMU's Global Sustainability School, which welcomes international undergraduate and postgraduate students and study-abroad groups; no background in the topic is needed.

Applications open on 1 March 2027.

en: Women's leadership and empowerment focus
Intercultural communication in northern Thailand
Accommodation and logistics included

Submit the online application form.
Pay the programme fee once accepted.
Book flights and arrange your Thai visa if needed.

costs.en: THB 45,000 including programme fees, 16 nights accommodation, logistics and some meals. Flights extra.

score_reason: Distinctive topic, affordable; few details published yet.

about.en:
The Student Leader Global Summit (SLGS) is the annual student-leadership event of IASAS, the international association of university student-affairs professionals. The 2027 summit is hosted in Manila, Philippines, by the Philippine Association of Campus Student Advisers (PACSA) from 26 to 29 May 2027 (the 2026 edition was in Hong Kong).

It brings together student leaders (student union, club and residence leaders and other active students) to connect across cultures, exchange ideas and develop leadership. Staff from your university's student-affairs office can accompany you.

In 2026 the fee (about EUR 290–320) covered three nights' accommodation, meals and materials; the 2027 fee is still to be confirmed.

en: Meet student leaders from universities worldwide
Hosted by the Philippine student-affairs association
Accommodation and meals included in the package (2026 model)

eligibility.en: University students active in student leadership; applicants usually apply with the support of their university student-affairs office.

Submit your application (reviews begin January 2027).
Confirm your place within a couple of weeks of acceptance.
Pay the registration fee a month before the event and book flights.

costs.en: Registration fee not yet confirmed (2026: EUR 290 members / EUR 320 non-members, including 3 nights, meals and materials). Flights extra.

score_reason: Genuine international student-leader summit; fee and deadline still pending.

about.en:
The SDG July Camp brings students from around the world to Shanghai Jiao Tong University to tackle sustainability challenges through the UN Sustainable Development Goals, with support from UNDP. Students choose one of several SDG-themed courses taught through group projects, discussions and public lectures by global experts.

The camp also includes an opening ceremony and icebreakers, weekly cross-cultural activities and a closing ceremony where each course presents its report. Completers receive a certificate and an SJTU transcript.

In 2026 applications ran from 15 January to 31 May, with admission decisions in early June and the opening ceremony on 14 July; the 2027 camp is expected on the same calendar.

en: SDG-focused, project-based courses with SJTU transcript
Supported by UNDP
Cultural activities in Shanghai

eligibility.en: University students from around the world interested in the SDGs (see the call for any GPA or language requirements).

Apply online at apply.sjtu.edu.cn before the end of May.
Wait for the admission decision (early June).
Apply for a Chinese visa with the admission documents.

costs.en: Fees are listed in the yearly call (not shown on the overview page). Travel and visa extra.

about.en:
Doshisha University's Center for Japanese Language and Culture runs a summer session in Kyoto each year (6 July – 5 August in 2026), combining intensive Japanese classes with cultural studies in one of Japan's most historic cities.

It is designed for students with JLPT N4 to N2 level (or equivalent); complete beginners and N1-level learners are not eligible. Applicants must be enrolled in, or graduates of, a university and able to obtain a visa. Places are limited to about 20.

The 2027 session is expected to open for applications in mid-January 2027 with a mid-March deadline.

en: Intensive Japanese in Kyoto
Small group (about 20 students)
Open to university students and graduates worldwide

eligibility.en: Undergraduate or graduate students, or university graduates, with JLPT N4–N2 or equivalent Japanese; must be able to get a visa if required.

en: Check the Summer Session page for the 2027 call (expected January).
Apply online with passport copy, motivation letter and letter of consent.
Receive results in late March.
Pay the programme fee in early April to complete registration.

costs.en: 2026 fee: JPY 250,000. Accommodation, travel and living costs extra.

score_reason: Solid Kyoto language course; needs prior Japanese.

The Global Collaborative (GC) Summer Program at Kyung Hee University, Seoul, offers English-taught, credit-bearing courses under the theme 'Humanity, Civilization and Global Governance', many taught by visiting professors from leading universities abroad.

Students from KHU partner universities and non-partner universities worldwide can join; students enrolled outside Korea pay overseas rates. Optional dormitory rooms and a Korean culture experience package are available.

The 2027 dates and application window will be published on the GC site (the 2026 cycle closed in June).

en: Courses by international visiting professors
Up to 6 transferable credits
Optional dorm and Korean culture package

eligibility.en: University students from partner and non-partner universities worldwide (see the GC site for detailed requirements).

en: Check summer.khu.ac.kr for the 2027 academic calendar.
Apply online and pay the KRW 100,000 application fee.
Pay tuition (and optional dorm/culture fees) by the payment deadline.
Email the payment receipt to summer@khu.ac.kr.

summary.ar: يقضي طلاب الدكتوراه من جامعات خارج سنغافورة سنة إلى سنتين في البحث بمعاهد A*STAR بإشراف مشترك، مع تغطية الراتب الشهري والسكن وتذكرة الطيران والتأمين وبدل المؤتمرات.

about.en:
The A*STAR Research Attachment Programme (ARAP) connects overseas universities with A*STAR, Singapore's lead public research agency. PhD (and postgraduate) students based at overseas universities spend 1–2 years in an A*STAR research institute working on a joint project under co-supervision by their home supervisor and an A*STAR researcher, in biomedical sciences, physical sciences, engineering, infocomm and related fields.

Students are nominated jointly by their home university and A*STAR supervisors. A*STAR researchers submit nominations by 1 June or 1 December each year, and attachments can start six months after the award. Applicants need at least a Second-Class Upper honours bachelor's degree (or equivalent), strong references and a good research record.

Awardees receive a monthly stipend and housing allowance, a one-time IT allowance, airfare grant and settling-in allowance, visa costs, medical insurance and a conference allowance.

en: Fully funded 1–2 year research stay in Singapore
Access to world-class A*STAR facilities
Two nomination rounds a year (1 June, 1 December)

eligibility.en: Overseas-based PhD/postgraduate students with at least a Second-Class Upper bachelor's degree (or equivalent), strong referees and a research track record, nominated jointly by their home university supervisor and an A*STAR supervisor. Students at ARAP partner universities contact their university's ARAP office.

en: Identify an A*STAR researcher whose work fits your PhD and discuss a joint project (with your home supervisor).
Check whether your university is on the ARAP partner list and contact its ARAP office.
The A*STAR supervisor submits the nomination by 1 December 2026 (or 1 June 2027).
If awarded, start the attachment about six months later.

costs.en: Fully funded: monthly stipend, monthly housing allowance, IT allowance, airfare grant, settling-in allowance, visa cost, medical insurance and conference allowance.

score_reason: Fully funded and prestigious; requires supervisor nomination.

org: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

name.ar: برنامج البحث الصيفي للطلاب الجامعيين في الجامعة الصينية بهونغ كونغ (SURP) 2027

duration.ka: 8 კვირა (2027 ივნისის ბოლო – აგვისტოს შუა რიცხვები)

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 (online application deadline 13 Feb 2026 for 21 Jun – 15 Aug); confirm the 2027 timeline on the official page.

summary.en: An eight-week, 3-credit research attachment at CUHK for senior undergraduates from overseas universities, with 160+ projects across all faculties and guaranteed campus housing. Up to 10 tuition waivers are offered.
summary.ka: რვაკვირიანი, 3-კრედიტიანი კვლევითი სტაჟირება CUHK-ში უცხოური უნივერსიტეტების უფროსკურსელი ბაკალავრებისთვის: 160-ზე მეტი პროექტი ყველა ფაკულტეტზე და გარანტირებული საცხოვრებელი კამპუსზე. გაიცემა 10-მდე სწავლის საფასურის გათავისუფლება.
summary.ar: إلحاق بحثي لمدة ثمانية أسابيع بثلاث ساعات معتمدة في الجامعة الصينية بهونغ كونغ لطلاب السنوات المتقدمة من جامعات خارجية، مع أكثر من 160 مشروعًا في جميع الكليات وسكن جامعي مضمون، وحتى 10 إعفاءات من الرسوم.

about.en:
SURP lets senior undergraduates from overseas (non-Chinese) universities spend eight weeks doing research under a CUHK faculty member, choosing from 160+ topics across science, engineering, medicine, business, social sciences and humanities. In 2026 it ran from 21 June to 15 August with about 180 students.

Participants register in a 3-credit course ('Independent Research on International Studies') and receive a transcript; they devote at least 20 hours a week to the project and join orientation, cultural activities and excursions. On-campus housing (shared rooms) is guaranteed.

You can apply as an exchange student (if nominated by a CUHK partner) or as a fee-paying student. In 2026 the online deadline was 13 February; up to 10 tuition waivers go to strong applicants, with priority for financial need.

en: 160+ research topics in every faculty
3 credits and a CUHK transcript
Up to 10 tuition waivers; guaranteed campus housing

eligibility.en: Full-time senior undergraduates in good academic standing at an overseas, non-Chinese university. English proof required if your university does not teach in English. Admission is decided by CUHK host supervisors.

en: Browse the SURP research project list and choose topics.
Prepare a recent academic recommendation letter, transcript, passport copy and (if needed) English proof.
Submit the online application by the February deadline (exchange students also need home-university endorsement).
Once admitted, pay fees and apply for a Hong Kong student visa (6–8 weeks).

costs.en: 2026 fee-paying students: tuition HK$8,150 (~US$1,050; up to 10 waivers), administration fee HK$4,000, optional on-campus housing HK$8,800, visa HK$100–730, refundable deposits. Exchange students: tuition waived. Travel and meals extra.

score_reason: Large, structured research programme open to any overseas university; moderate fees.

org: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

name.en: CUHK Summer Institute 2027 for Secondary School Students
name.ka: CUHK-ის საზაფხულო ინსტიტუტი 2027 საშუალო სკოლის მოსწავლეებისთვის
name.ar: المعهد الصيفي للجامعة الصينية بهونغ كونغ 2027 لطلاب المدارس الثانوية

deadline_note: Estimated from 2026 (non-local early-bird/merit deadline 27 Mar, general deadline 10 Apr 2026; applications open early March).

summary.en: A two-week residential programme where secondary students (about Grade 11 / IB DP1, 16+) take one or two university courses taught by CUHK scholars and can earn credit towards future CUHK study. Merit awards halve the fee.
summary.ka: ორკვირიანი პროგრამა საცხოვრებლით, სადაც საშუალო სკოლის მოსწავლეები (დაახლოებით მე-11 კლასი / IB DP1, 16+) CUHK-ის მეცნიერების ერთ ან ორ საუნივერსიტეტო კურსს გადიან და შეუძლიათ კრედიტის მიღება მომავალი სწავლისთვის. დამსახურების ჯილდო საფასურს ანახევრებს.
summary.ar: برنامج سكني لمدة أسبوعين يدرس فيه طلاب الثانوية (نحو الصف الحادي عشر / السنة الأولى من IB، بعمر 16+) مقررًا أو مقررين جامعيين على يد أساتذة الجامعة، مع إمكانية احتساب ساعات معتمدة للدراسة المستقبلية فيها. تخفض منح الجدارة الرسوم إلى النصف.

about.en:
The CUHK Summer Institute (SI) is a two-week summer programme for secondary school students who will apply to university the following year. Students take one or two short academic courses from 20+ options taught by 40+ CUHK scholars, join orientation and enrichment activities, and experience campus life with 350+ local and international participants.

It is open to Grade 11 (American system), Year 12 (A-level), IB DP year 1, Gaokao Senior 2, Taiwanese Senior 2 and equivalent international curricula, aged 16+ at the start. Credits can count towards future undergraduate study at CUHK (terms apply).

Non-local students live on campus. Merit awards (for students recognised by gifted-education bodies or recommended by their school) halve the programme fee.

en: University courses taught by CUHK scholars
Credits towards future CUHK study
Merit awards cut the fee by half

eligibility.en: Secondary students applying to university in 2028 (e.g. Grade 11, A-level Year 12, IB DP1, or equivalent), aged 16+ when the programme starts. Any nationality.

en: Choose one or two courses from the SI course list.
Create an account in the online application system (opens early March) and upload your last two school reports.
Apply for a merit award (school recommendation) by the early-bird deadline if eligible.
Pay the HK$150 application fee within two days; accept the offer and pay fees within four days of results.

costs.en: 2026 non-local: two courses HK$9,200 (early bird HK$8,740; merit award HK$4,600), accommodation HK$3,300, activities HK$1,600, visa HK$100–730, application fee HK$150. Flights extra.

score_reason: Strong pre-university programme for international high-schoolers with merit discounts.

org: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST)

name.ar: برنامج الطالب الباحث الزائر في UNIST

deadline_note: Rolling: apply at least 45 days before your desired research start date (official UNIST page).

summary.en: Students from outside Korea can join a research lab at UNIST, one of Korea's top science and technology institutes, once a professor agrees to host them. Applications are rolling, 45 days before the start date.
summary.ka: კორეის გარეთ მყოფ სტუდენტებს შეუძლიათ UNIST-ის — კორეის ერთ-ერთი წამყვანი სამეცნიერო-ტექნოლოგიური ინსტიტუტის — ლაბორატორიაში მუშაობა, თუ პროფესორი მასპინძლობაზე თანახმაა. განაცხადი მიიღება მუდმივად, დაწყებამდე 45 დღით ადრე.
summary.ar: يمكن للطلاب من خارج كوريا الانضمام إلى مختبر بحثي في UNIST، أحد أبرز معاهد العلوم والتكنولوجيا في كوريا، بعد موافقة أستاذ على استضافتهم. التقديم مفتوح طوال العام قبل 45 يومًا من تاريخ البدء.

about.en:
The Visiting Research Student (VRS) Program at UNIST in Ulsan is for students from outside South Korea who want to carry out research in one of UNIST's laboratories (energy, materials, chemistry, biomedical engineering, AI, semiconductors and more).

There is no fixed intake: you contact the laboratory you want to join, obtain permission from the professor in charge, and then apply at least 45 days before your desired start date. Accepted students obtain a D-2-5 research-student visa using UNIST's documents and proof of funds (bank statement or research stipend).

It suits undergraduate, master's and PhD students who already have a potential host professor, for example for a thesis project or summer research.

en: Year-round, flexible research stays
Work in labs at a top Korean science university
Good way to meet a future graduate supervisor

eligibility.en: Students based outside South Korea who have secured permission from a UNIST professor to host them. Proof of funding (bank balance or stipend) is required for the visa.

en: Find a UNIST lab that fits your interests and email the professor.
Once the professor agrees, apply to the International Affairs Team at least 45 days before your start date.
Receive UNIST documents and apply for a D-2-5 visa at your nearest Korean mission.
Arrange health insurance and housing (on-campus guest house or off-campus).

costs.en: Costs depend on the host lab (some labs offer stipends); visa fees, travel, insurance and living costs are usually your own unless the lab funds them.

score_reason: Flexible year-round access to Korean labs; you must find a host yourself.
